rules.statement: When a package owns an exception that can escape a protocol endpoint, map it to a protocol error with a translator the package registers through `TryAddEnumerable` in an open collection, not with a hard-coded `switch` or type check in the core library.
rules.why: A closed mapping in core can't cover exceptions that other packages own. An open collection, where the first translator that answers wins and anything unanswered becomes `server_error`, lets a package add its exceptions without changing core.
rules.check: Look for new package-owned exception types that can reach protocol endpoints with no translator registered for them, for core code that special-cases another package's exception type, and for translators registered with `Add` instead of `TryAddEnumerable`.

rules.statement: Answer a temporary condition that a retry resolves on a protocol endpoint with `temporarily_unavailable`, status 503, a `Retry-After` header in whole seconds rounded up to at least 1, and `Cache-Control: no-store`, not with `server_error`.
rules.why: With `server_error`, a client can't tell a temporary outage that a retry fixes from a fault. Every protocol endpoint answers temporary conditions the same way.
rules.check: Check that outage or throttling paths on protocol endpoints return `temporarily_unavailable` with 503, set `Retry-After` by rounding the configured interval up (ceiling, minimum 1, never truncated to 0), and set `Cache-Control: no-store`.

rules.statement: In the authorization endpoint's catch-all, translate the exception into a protocol error and deliver it to the client's redirect URI with `state`, as RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1 requires, instead of letting it escape as a generic server error.
rules.why: A client of the authorization endpoint must receive the error at its redirect URI along with `state`.
rules.check: Check the authorization request processor's generic exception handling: does it run the exception translators and redirect with `error` and `state`?

rules.statement: Translate an exception into a protocol error before choosing the exception handler, so that endpoint-specific handlers receive the translated protocol exception and not the raw package-owned exception.
rules.why: Endpoint-specific handlers should see the same protocol exception that every other endpoint would answer with.
rules.check: In endpoint exception filters or middleware, check that translation happens before the handler is chosen or the exception is audited.

rules.statement: Log a `temporarily_unavailable` protocol error at Warning with its own event ID, not at Error.
rules.why: The condition is resolved by the tenant or the environment and isn't a defect of the server.
rules.check: Look at the log level used for temporarily-unavailable or outage errors in exception handlers.
